news.2026-11-21-finlande-cargo-russe-spa: Gulf of Finland: a military-linked Russian cargo ship hit by drones drifts ablaze into Finnish waters, Helsinki alerts NATO

On Saturday, November 21, the Sparta II, a Russian cargo ship under US sanctions bound for Kaliningrad, caught fire after being hit by two drones in the eastern Gulf of Finland. It drifted into Finnish waters off Loviisa, and Finland informed NATO [1][3][6].

According to Alexander Drozdenko, governor of Russia's Leningrad region, two drones struck the ship in international waters, about three nautical miles from the Russian maritime border; the crew was evacuated and the damage was being assessed [1][3].

Finland's Defence Ministry says it detected a drone attack on a Russian cargo ship west of the island of Suursaari [2]. According to Estonian authorities, the vessel was sailing in an international shipping lane 11 nautical miles north of the Estonian island of Vaindloo [5].

The Sparta II, a Russian-flagged roll-on/roll-off ship, is operated by Oboronlogistics, a company linked to the Russian Defence Ministry; it has been under US sanctions since May 2022 and is also sanctioned by Ukraine [3][4].

Once hit, the ship lost steering control and drifted into Finnish territorial waters south of Loviisa, where the Finnish Border Guard is leading the rescue and efforts against possible pollution [4][6].

The commander of the Finnish Border Guard, Ilja Iljin, told broadcaster Yle that Ukrainian drones hit the cargo ship while it was in Russian waters, and that it "could be carrying military equipment" [4]. The Finnish armed forces consider it likely that Ukraine was behind the attack, without knowing why this ship was targeted [3].

No one has claimed the attack, and Ukraine's Foreign Ministry did not immediately respond [3]. Kaliningrad's governor, Alexei Besprozvannykh, says the incident does not threaten supplies to the exclave [3].

Finland's Defence Minister, Antti Häkkänen, said a Russian helicopter may have entered Finnish airspace by 4.1 km off Loviisa, probably during rescue or monitoring operations around the cargo ship [7].
The key point: the war between Russia and Ukraine is reaching the waters of a NATO country, in the heart of the Baltic, the day after Russian missiles fell in Poland [6].

"The war is spilling over into our neighbouring regions," summed up Finnish Prime Minister Petteri Orpo [6]. Helsinki twice imposed temporary restrictions on air and sea traffic in the eastern Gulf of Finland as a precaution [4].

The Gulf of Finland is St Petersburg's sea access, and Kaliningrad, wedged between Poland and Lithuania, partly depends on these sea links [2][3]. An attack on this route therefore hits a sensitive corridor for Moscow, right next to Finland and Estonia, both NATO members [5][6].

For you, it shows that the war in Ukraine is getting closer to European Union countries, this time by sea. The Baltic is an important route for European trade and undersea cables: if incidents multiply there, NATO and the EU, France included, could step up their military presence.
